# Can the complete F be sent? (P2-R9 items 3-5)

**Question.** can the complete F message (all 55 blocks) be delivered inside one 100 ms frame period, and does a continuous 10 Hz stream backlog?

**Subject.** F = the complete bottleneck of the frozen checkpoint, existing compression and int8 quantisation unchanged; L = the object-level message; E = ego-only. Nothing about F was changed for this audit.

## 3 The payload chain, re-derived and checked

| step | value | basis |
|---|---:|---|
| bottleneck elements | 739,200 | forward-hook probe of the frozen checkpoint |
| quantisation width (bits/element) | 8 | symmetric int8, per-branch pre-shared scales |
| information bits | 5,913,600 | elements x width |
| full packets | 739 | payload 8,000 bits each |
| tail packet payload bits | 1,600 | the tail packet is not padded to a full payload |
| packets | 740 | full packets + tail |
| header bits | 236,800 | 320 bits per packet |
| LDPC codewords | 12,567 | rate 1/2, K = 500, n = 1000, per packet, padded |
| coded bits | 12,567,000 | codewords x n |
| QAM data symbols | 3,141,750 | coded bits / log2(16) |
| Msym (QAM data symbols) | 3.14175 | the unit the protocol calls a channel use |

Every step agrees with the recorded product: {'elements': True, 'info_bits': True, 'packets': True, 'header_bits': True, 'n_cw': True, 'msym': True}.

**QAM symbols are not OFDM symbols.** A QAM data symbol occupies one data subcarrier of one OFDM symbol. An OFDM symbol carries as many QAM symbols as it has data subcarriers, so the two counts differ by that factor and only the OFDM count has a duration. 3.14175 Msym is the QAM count; it is not a symbol time and not an OFDM count.

## 5 Verdict

**0 of 27 configurations can deliver the complete F inside 100 ms.**

The best row is NR sidelink 40 MHz / 15 kHz, idealised upper bound: 101.0 ms, 1.01× the frame period, so a 10 Hz stream of complete F messages backlogs without bound; the highest rate it could sustain is 9.90 Hz. L finishes in about a millisecond everywhere and never backlogs.

**Candidates for a degradation experiment:** none.

**Where the deficit sits.** message size: the complete F needs 3.14175 Msym, while the widest configuration examined delivers at most 3.11040 Msym in a 100 ms period even with no overhead at all. The deficit at the best row is a factor of 1.01, and every configuration with stated overhead is worse. The frame period and the resource grid are what they are; what does not fit is the message.

*no sparse F, no transmission spread across frames and no lower sending rate is proposed here; this audit reports feasibility only.*

## Assumptions that do not match a standard link

* the P1 chain fixes a rate-1/2 LDPC with K = 500 and n = 1000; that is not the code either standard specifies, and no standard code was substituted, so the codeword count is not a standard block segmentation.
* modulation is fixed at 16-QAM regardless of channel quality; neither standard's MCS set is used.
* one P1 channel use is mapped to one data resource element of the standard grid.
* the 320-bit header models IP/UDP/application overhead only; no MAC framing of either standard is charged.
* the idealised arm gives the whole carrier to one link, continuously, with no preamble, contention, queueing or retransmission.
* the 802.11bd tone count and symbol period come from patent text (IEEE 802.11bd-2022 is paywalled); the midamble arm assumes one NGV-LTF symbol per midamble.
* n47 bandwidths and subcarrier spacings are verified against TS 38.101-1 V17.0.0 Table 5.3.5-1.
